title: What can it read? Sandboxing the agent
part: Part 3 · AI as your co-admin, behind gates
brief: A sandbox that reads your whole home directory is not a sandbox. Deny the credential paths by name, allow the registries by name, and prove both before the agent starts.

exercises.prompt: Claude Code's sandbox docs say reads cover the entire machine except denied directories. Which files stay readable unless you deny them?
options: Nothing; reads are blocked by default
exercises.explain: The docs: credential files such as ~/.ssh remain readable unless you deny them. srt follows the same model. The repo's srt-settings.json denies every credential path by name and by pattern.

exercises.prompt: On Ubuntu 24.04 and later the sandbox fails before it starts. Why, and what does the repo do about it?
options: bwrap is not packaged; the repo compiles it
AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces; the repo installs a profile allowing bwrap specifically instead of disabling the restriction globally
Docker conflicts with bwrap; the repo removes Docker
exercises.explain: Disabling the user-namespace restriction host-wide would weaken every other process. A per-binary AppArmor profile is the minimal change.

exercises.prompt: run-sandboxed.sh runs its checks before launching the agent. One of them must SUCCEED. Which?
exercises.explain: A sandbox that blocks everything is a sandbox the agent will be told to turn off. The allowlist must still let it reach the package registries.

exercises.prompt: In the Docker agent box, the container sits on an 'internal' network. How does it reach PyPI at all?
options: Through a squid proxy with a domain allowlist, which also logs every attempt
exercises.explain: No default route; the only way out is the proxy, and the proxy log is your record of what the agent tried to reach, independent of what the agent says it did.

exercises.prompt: This sandbox config lets the agent go anywhere and read almost everything. Allow only localhost, the package registries and GitHub; deny the cloud metadata endpoint; deny reads of credential directories and token or .env files; keep writes to the project and /tmp/agent-work.
exercises.hint: Replace "*" with explicit domains (pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, registry.npmjs.org, github.com, ...), add 169.254.169.254 to deniedDomains, add ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.config/gh, **/.env and **/*token* to denyRead, drop ~ from allowWrite, and delete the _todo key. It must stay valid JSON.
exercises.explain: This is a trimmed version of the track's sandbox/srt-settings.json. Then prove it: make sandbox-verify must show the credential read and the metadata request failing and PyPI succeeding.

checks.name: package registries and GitHub still reachable
writes stay in the project and /tmp/agent-work

exercises.prompt: Install the sandbox settings for real and run the five checks. Cleared when ~/.srt-settings.json exists.
exercises.hint: 02-agents.sh copies sandbox/srt-settings.json to ~/.srt-settings.json. Do not run the agent if sandbox-verify reports a failure.
